q: Are urea, DAP and other fertilisers covered by EU CBAM?
title: Are urea and DAP covered by CBAM?
short: Yes. Nitrogenous fertilisers under CN 3102, which includes urea, and mixed fertilisers under 3105, which includes DAP, are in Annex I of the EU CBAM Regulation, as are ammonia (2814) and nitric acid (2808). Potash under 3104 and single superphosphate under 3103 are not covered.
audience: Fertiliser producers and traders exporting to the EU

ul: 3102: mineral or chemical fertilisers, nitrogenous, such as urea, ammonium nitrate and ammonium sulphate.
3105: fertilisers with two or three of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, such as DAP and NPK, except 3105 60 00 (phosphorus and potassium only).
3103: phosphatic fertilisers such as single superphosphate.
3104: potassic fertilisers such as muriate of potash.

p: For fertilisers, CBAM counts both direct emissions and the indirect emissions from electricity used in production. Nitrous oxide from nitric acid production is included, so abatement there matters for the figure.
Since the 2025 amendment, an importer bringing in no more than 50 tonnes a year of CBAM goods, other than hydrogen and electricity, is exempt. Large fertiliser consignments usually exceed that.
